column3: Shows fear addressed to the Rabb amid immediate danger, a distinct but related fear register.
Adds a public face-outcome contrast that can sit alongside the day's frowning face.
Frames fear for others as protective anticipation of a great coming day, with both Rabb-relation and action-moving readings.
Names the same feared day as widespread evil and makes that fear the lead-in to present faithfulness and giving.
Supplies the sequel: protection from that day's evil and a counter-reception of radiance and joy.
Adds an appointed day that cannot be advanced or delayed, whether read as date or constraining event.
Uses day only for a short duration, adding little to the feared-day scene.
Places the feeding named by 76:10 directly before its stated motive.
Shows fear disclosed to the Rabb as a real obstacle to a mission, distinct from fear of the day.
Shows an appeal to the Rabb for relief from punishment, supporting the restorative-address reading without the day imagery.
Provides the bright-face counterpart to a day marked by facial severity.
Offers facial contraction and turning away as an immediate bodily scene; a secondary anticipatory-face reading also remains possible.
Depicts sufferers asking their Rabb for even one day of relief from punishment.
Begins the surrounding portrait of the righteous whose later fear and reception are described.
States fear of disobeying one's Rabb and a great day; it can be both moral restraint and loss of the Rabb-relation.
Calls the day hard for disbelievers and assigns true rule to the Merciful.
Concerns receiving the Quran from the Wise, Knowing source; only an indirect warning-context resonance.
Identifies the Rabb of Moses and Aaron but adds no fear or day dimension.
Pairs frowning with another facial tightening, supporting the pressure-in-the-face aspect without fixing its scope.
Makes the day an appointed collective time of separation, reinforcing its judicial and gathered character.
Shows the day as a setting of isolation and deprivation, extending its severe social consequences.
Links a messenger's warning to regret before humiliation, but not directly to 76:10's feared day.
Connects the surah to revelation, with no direct contribution to fear, face, or day.
Presents fear of the Rabb's standing as conduct-shaping; both judgment and abiding-presence senses remain open.
Shows the event's arrival converting neglected warning into regret and a wish for different action.
Describes a destined encounter with a day of overwhelming shock, adding an encounter dimension.
Shows future-oriented fear generating protective, just action for vulnerable others.
Links fear of a day that overturns hearts and eyes to sustained worship and almsgiving.
Gives the immediate declaration of disinterested feeding that 76:10 explains.
Portrays warning others out of concern for a great day, a parallel protective-fear stance.
Adds trust and return to the Rabb, but no focused day or facial severity.
Combines Quran recitation with warning, only indirectly related to the fear's action-producing role.
Affirms the Rabb's governance of a named star, remote from the day and fear scene.
Adds collective gathering, fixed term, and final address to the Rabb as dimensions of the day.
Adds the surah's temporal human prelude, not the feared future event.
Shows the day overturning ordinary kinship through flight from one's brother.
The statement of incurred loss adds no clear focus-specific element.
Names a promised day belonging to deniers, making future threat determinate.
Contrasts the fear and grief removed through piety and repair with the fear articulated in 76:10.
Distinguishes imminent fear and grief from rescue assurance, a separate danger-and-protection pattern.
Continues the surah's response to patient righteousness with garden and silk.
Calls the day great and situates it within an accountability horizon.
Shows fear answered by a promise that redirects present action toward a future restoration.
Presents revelation as warning, but does not specify 76:10's fear or severe day.
Describes rupture or redirected attachment toward the Rabb, only indirectly relevant to fear's Rabb-relation.
Faces threat through return to the Rabb, an alternative outcome-oriented posture.
Develops the surah's source-and-drinking imagery rather than the feared day.
Sets freedom from fear and grief in closeness to Allah, a counter-state to 76:10's fear.
Reorients desire after loss toward the Rabb who can replace, indirectly paralleling corrective response.
Shows questioning the day's timing as a possible challenge to accountability, alongside the fixed-day reading.
Depicts situational fear as watchfulness, unlike the future-day fear in 76:10.
Restates fear of disobeying the Rabb and punishment on a great day as measured moral foresight.
Adds regular remembrance of the Rabb later in the same surah, supporting an ongoing relational dimension.
Shows a day of total submission after mutual support fails, adding a collective collapse scene.
Frames mortal threat within return to the Rabb, without resolving the precise nature of that return.
Associates the Rabb with provision and security, a possible background for worship and giving rather than a day description.
Sets false appeals against a final gathering when real positions are exposed.
Affirms the Rabb's promise as fulfilled, with only broad relevance to a feared future.
Places prepared chains, shackles, and blaze in the surah's prior punishment horizon.
Makes the Rabb fully aware of people on that day, adding inward accountability to the outcome.
Depicts rapid emergence from the earth for an easy gathering, adding concrete assembly imagery.
Limits knowledge of the future to Allah and defines the speaker as a clear warner.
Contrasts fear directed by rivals with fear directed to Allah, keeping the fear object's orientation in view.
Directly voices fear for a people of a named day of calling, a close parallel to 76:10.
Adds the surah's testing-of-humanity frame but not the specific feared day.
Uses fear for others and historical precedent to make anticipated consequence ethically operative now.
Pairs exclusive worship with warning others of a painful day, closely paralleling the verse's concern for a coming day.
Turns warning into an anticipated destructive event, supporting the future-harm dimension without the same day language.
Treats delay as movement toward a specified day rather than cancellation of accountability.
Combines return to the Rabb with hope for forgiveness, a reparative counterpoint to anticipated punishment.
Names the record of the righteous, only broadly adjacent to 76's portrait of the righteous.
Sets activity within a known, fixed temporal limit, supporting the appointed-boundary aspect of a day.
States that the Rabb's punishment is not safely assumed away, sustaining vigilance.
Shows fear reading a remaining sign as warning of future painful punishment.
Appeals to the Rabb's knowledge to validate a mission, not directly to the feared day.
Names measured recompense from the Rabb; it can be read as personal gift within wider governance.
Supplies chains and blazing fire as a punishment backdrop, without the day designation.
Defines the Day of Recompense as lived consequence, while retaining the secondary open-time sense.
The declaration of non-worship adds no clear focus-specific contribution.
Names the Day of Separation, where distinction yields outcomes after gathering.
Shows confession of wrongdoing and exoneration of the Rabb after loss, a corrective response pattern.
Emphasizes the Day of Recompense's gravity and incomprehensibility, with both event and open-time readings retained.
Confesses the revealed truth as from the Rabb, but adds no focused fear or day element.
Contrasts the absence of fear and grief with belief in Allah, the last day, and righteous action.
Shows the Rabb's word becoming an experienced consequence, though without the specific day scene.
Treats resurrection as a requested deadline for continued activity, only loosely related to 76:10.
Links hope for entry among the righteous to belief and received truth from the Rabb.
Shows fear of a real threat presented to the Rabb and met later by support, distinct from eschatological fear.
Adds a prayer for family joy and leadership among the mindful, only indirectly aligned with present righteous action.
Identifies denial of the Day of Recompense as part of the path toward its consequences.
Prays for rescue from disbelieving people, without the day or facial focus.
Describes mercy from the Rabb in a warning setting, but not 76:10's specific relation.
The statement about inability to be patient adds no clear focus-specific element.
Uses resurrection as a long temporal endpoint, not the severe day under discussion.
Supplies concrete ethical commands under the Rabb's authority, including care amid poverty, relevant to present conduct.
Shows anticipatory fear regulating a just, disclosed response rather than panic or covert retaliation.
The command not to obey deniers adds no clear focus-specific element.
Calls for recognition of the Rabb's favors, only broadly related to grateful righteous response.
Forbids transgression in the balance, an ethical parallel without fear or day content.
Attributes escape from being brought forth to the Rabb's favor, adding a protection-from-peril counterpart.
Makes return to Allah and full requital the future horizon that can govern present action.
Shows each soul confronting its deeds and wishing its evil were distant, adding personal anticipatory consequence.
Frames final success as being moved away from the Fire and admitted to the Garden.
Adds a day of witnesses and testimony, extending the public-accountability dimension.
Depicts Allah gathering the messengers on the day, giving the feared event a collective judicial setting.
Shows all being gathered and false associations exposed on a day of reckoning.
Links loss at meeting Allah to regret and burdens carried, a consequence-focused future scene.
Adds weighing on the day as a measure-bearing form of accountability.
Depicts universal gathering and separation from false partners, extending the day as disclosure.
Names a day for which people are gathered and witnessed, directly strengthening the collective-event reading.
Portrays speech and human division under the Lord's permission on the day it arrives.
Keeps divine forbearance from being mistaken for neglect before a day of fixed consequences.
Commands warning people of the day punishment comes, closely matching fear made present by warning.
Shows every soul pleading for itself and receiving full recompense, adding individual accountability.
Commands warning of the Day of Regret while people remain heedless, a direct future-warning parallel.
Shows all following the caller on a day when voices are hushed, adding gathered submission.
Places humbled faces before the Living, Sustaining One, closely paralleling facial severity and outcome.
Calls the convulsion of the Hour a tremendous thing, intensifying the severe-event dimension.
Shows kinship ties and mutual questioning failing when the trumpet is blown.
Adds bodily testimony by tongues, hands, and feet on the day of full recompense.
Depicts the day angels are seen as bad news for criminals, adding an adverse encounter.
Shows regret on the day the wrongdoer bites his hands, a personal response to disclosed loss.
Describes the trumpet day as one of terror, with all arriving humbled before Allah.
Adds divine calling and exposure of claimed partners on the day of questioning.
Shows a day when messengers are called and answers fail, extending judgment's public questioning.
Calls for turning to the upright way before an irreversible day arrives.
Shows rapid emergence from graves toward the Lord after the trumpet, giving the day a concrete summons.
Supplies blackened faces on the Day of Resurrection, a strong counterpart to the frowning-face register.
Portrays the approaching day with hearts at throats and no protecting ally, intensifying constricted severity.
Continues the Day of Calling with flight and no protector from Allah, directly elaborating 40:32.
Provides the counter-address of no fear or grief for Allah's servants.
Shows a day when no close relation can avail another, adding the collapse of ordinary protection.
Places judgment among Allah's dominion on the day the Hour rises and falsifiers lose.
Names the trumpet blast as the promised day, joining warning to an irreversible arrival.
Shows the sky violently shaken on the day of the threatened consequence.
Depicts humbled eyes and dispersed emergence from graves at a day of harsh summons.
Shows a dividing barrier between believers and hypocrites on the day, extending separation and loss.
Names the Day of Gathering as the day of mutual loss and gain, directly clarifying collective outcome.
Begins the trumpet sequence that makes the day an overwhelming cosmic and judicial event.
States that on that day people are displayed and no secret remains hidden.
Shows the sky becoming like molten metal on the day, extending the event's cosmic severity.
Shows intimate friends unable to ask about one another, paralleling the day’s social rupture.
Depicts hurried emergence from graves toward a fixed marker, giving the day a gathered movement.
Calls the day one that makes children gray-haired, directly paralleling severe future calamity.
Introduces the trumpet-blast day as a hard, non-easy day for disbelievers.
Gives bright faces on that day, a direct counterpoint to 76:10's frowning face.
Gives faces darkened by expectation of a crushing fate, closely aligned with facial severity.
Makes fear of standing before the Rabb restrain desire, a close action-producing fear parallel.
Introduces bright laughing, rejoicing faces on that day as a counter-reception.
Gives faces covered with dust and darkness, strongly extending the adverse face register.
Begins the cosmic unmaking associated with recompense, supplying the event's wider setting.
Begins the sky's opening and earth's response, adding cosmic manifestation of the final event.
Shows the earth crushed and the Lord's command arriving in ranks, a severe-arrival scene.
Shows people issuing forth separately to be shown their deeds, making consequences publicly enacted.
States that even an atom's weight of good will be seen, sharpening the action-consequence link.
States that even an atom's weight of evil will be seen, sharpening the feared consequence link.
Depicts people scattered like moths on the overwhelming Day of the Striking Calamity.
Names the abyss as the outcome of a light balance, adding a concrete adverse result.
Warns of a day when no soul can answer for another and intercession or ransom fails.
Repeats the no-substitution, no-ransom warning, reinforcing personal responsibility on the day.
Places the end of trading, friendship, and intercession before the coming day.
Assures universal gathering on the Day of Resurrection, supporting the collective scope of the feared day.
Presents the Hour as weighty in the heavens and earth and suddenly arriving.
Shows gathered people regarding worldly duration as brief, intensifying the encounter's perspective.
Depicts transformed earth and heavens when all stand before the One, Overpowering Allah.
Shows every people called with its record on a day of individualized public accounting.
Shows mountains removed, earth laid bare, and all gathered with none left behind.
Depicts the mindful gathered to the Most Merciful as a delegation, a favorable collective counterpart.
Depicts criminals driven to Hell thirsty, an adverse gathered counterpart.
Sets just balances for the Day of Resurrection and makes even the smallest deed count.
Provides the counter-state in which the greatest terror does not grieve the protected.
Shows the Hour's terror disorienting nursing mothers, children, and observers.
Makes heavy scales the basis of successful outcome after the trumpet.
Makes light scales the basis of self-loss, complementing the feared harm.
Shows the sky split by clouds and angels sent down on the day, adding an unveiled-arrival scene.
Adds burdens and burdens with burdens on the Day of Resurrection, connecting conduct to carried consequence.
Shows criminals despairing when the Hour is established.
Gives a day of meeting marked by peace for the faithful, a counter-reception to severe fear.
States that no soul is wronged and all are recompensed precisely for what they did.
Has people call the event the Day of Judgment when it arrives.
Names it the Day of Separation that had been denied, directly paralleling separation-day readings.
Shows the trumpet, death, rising, and waiting before the Lord in a single day-event sequence.
Shows the earth shining by its Lord's light as records and witnesses are set for judgment.
Names the Day of Meeting and connects it to warning of the Day of Mutual Calling.
States that each soul is repaid that day, with no injustice and swift reckoning.
Shows the wrongdoers humbled and looking furtively at punishment when the Hour is seen.
Shows intimate friends becoming enemies on that day except the mindful.
Shows every community kneeling and called to its record on the day of recompense.
Shows every soul arriving with a driver and a witness, giving judgment a personal procedural form.
Describes the veil removed and sight sharpened on the day, a disclosure counterpart to face imagery.
Adds mountains passing away during the threatened day.
Shows people thrust toward Hell's fire on that day.
Commands turning away until the caller summons to a terrible matter.
Gathers former and later peoples to the appointment of a known day.
Shows believers' light running before them and at their right hands on the day.
Shows Allah raising all and informing them of what they did, with deeds fully enumerated.
Shows a day when all are raised and speak falsely before Allah as they did in life.
Links denial of resurrection with the certainty of being raised and informed of deeds.
Shows the favorable reception of the record in the right hand after the day-event.
Shows the adverse reception of the record in the left hand after the day-event.
Adds humbled eyes and rushing emergence from graves on the promised day.
Completes the adverse-face scene with expectation of a crushing calamity.
Emphasizes the magnitude and incomprehensibility of the Day of Separation.
Names the trumpet day when people come in crowds.
Shows Spirit and angels standing in ranks, with speech restricted by the Most Merciful.
Begins the day with the first quake and its following quake.
Shows hearts trembling on that day, extending the inward constriction of the feared event.
Shows eyes lowered on that day, adding a visual counterpart to the face register.
Names the overwhelming calamity as the point when people remember their striving.
Shows records spread open within the final disclosure sequence.
Reiterates the question of what can make known the Day of Recompense, intensifying its gravity.
Shows people standing before the Lord of all worlds on the great day.
Shows the favorable receipt of one's record in the right hand.
Shows the adverse receipt of one's record from behind the back.
Names faces humbled on that day, a close adverse-face parallel.
Names faces joyful on that day, a close favorable-face counterpart.
Shows Hell brought near on that day and belated human remembrance.
Shows graves overturned on the day of full disclosure.
Shows what is in breasts brought out, adding inner exposure to the day of reckoning.
